# Doppel 2.2.0
- Each ChatGPT and Claude instance now has a Browser section with its own Chrome profile. The profile stays tied to the instance when you rename it, and your main Chrome is not touched. Claude One, for example, gets a Claude Code launch command that uses its own configuration folder. - You confirm that the app and its browser are signed in to the same account before Doppel shows connection steps or pairs the ChatGPT extension. Existing standalone profiles are kept and can be linked to an instance once the profile is closed. Doppel never deletes browser data. - The profile that runs on the official ChatGPT app is now called the official engine, and `doppel engine` replaces `doppel browser` (the old name still works). That profile is the only one that can use appshots and Computer history, because ChatGPT only accepts those from its own signed app. The in-app browser works in every instance.

# Doppel 2.1.1
- Doppel can update to ChatGPT 26.1027 and newer again. That build changed how the app is packaged, and Doppel refused to update with "this ChatGPT build is not compatible with Doppel yet". Your existing ChatGPT apps were never touched and kept working. - Doppel is now less likely to break the next time ChatGPT repackages itself. A plain change in how the app writes its code no longer stops an update. - Developers can run `just qa-vendor` to check the installed and any downloaded ChatGPT build against Doppel before applying an update.

# Doppel 2.1.0
Create separate Claude desktop apps from New Instance → Claude, each with its own login, Code configuration, name and colour. Google sign-in returns to the right instance, and Claude's pale star stays visible on tinted icons.
After signing in and opening Code, use Import Existing Code History to bring over local conversations for the same account and workspace. Existing sessions and original files are kept. Missing transcripts and working folders are reported. Working copies are not moved, so check the original folder for uncommitted work if Claude creates a new worktree when resuming a conversation.
